learningObjective: Enumerate the correct properties of mixed-precision Tensor Core GEMM: FP16/BF16 inputs with FP32 accumulator.

canonicalClaims.claim: Mixed-precision Tensor Core GEMM stores inputs in FP16/BF16 (halving memory bandwidth vs FP32) but accumulates in FP32 for numerical stability; downcasting the FP32 accumulator to FP16/BF16 on write adds a per-element rounding error.
conditions: The workload uses HMMA/BMMA Tensor Core kernels.
The framework respects the accumulator/output dtype configuration.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP32 accumulator eliminates all numerical issues.
Does not imply FP32 output is free — it doubles output storage.

misconceptions.claim: Because the accumulator is FP32, mixed-precision Tensor Core GEMM has the same throughput as pure FP32 GEMM.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Tensor Core throughput for mixed precision is 8-16× FP32 depending on generation; the accumulator width is not the bottleneck.

misconceptions.claim: Writing FP32 output has no storage overhead compared to FP16 output.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP32 is 4 bytes/element; FP16 is 2 bytes/element. Output storage doubles.

misconceptions.claim: The downcast on write is bit-exact and introduces no error.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Downcasting FP32 to FP16/BF16 rounds each element; error is bounded by half an ULP of the target format.

misconceptions.claim: Mixed precision only saves memory footprint, not memory bandwidth.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Halving element size halves both footprint and bandwidth; bandwidth is often the dominant end-to-end speed factor.

implementationFacts: cuBLAS Tensor Core GEMM: `computeType = CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F` with FP16 inputs.
PyTorch autocast wraps ops that support FP16/BF16 while keeping FP32 for the accumulator.
performanceScenarios: For a Transformer FFN, switching from FP32 to FP16 mixed precision typically yields 2-3× wall-clock speedup — dominated by bandwidth halving.
